advisories.title: G16 v2 is described as the 'Live G16 specification' without its CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED standing, while the other cited artifact's standing is quoted in full
advisories.detail: basedOn.g16v2.role reads 'Live G16 specification. namedCorpusNotAuthored and namedCorpusClasses are quoted. doesNotApplyV16 true.' G16 v2 is in fact CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL. None of that is recorded. The contrast is inside the same artifact: v16, which the catalog must not apply, gets its standing quoted verbatim as 'CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. binds NOTHING … Cited. Not applied', while G16 v2, whose bytes the catalog actually depends on, gets the single word 'Live'.
advisories.whyItStaysAdvisory: Nothing the catalog claims depends on G16 v2 being applied. It binds NOTHING itself, refuses to apply v16, refuses to close OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING, and refuses to SATISFY DR-121. It also pins G16 v2's review by path and digest and states the verdict including 'Codex not reviewed', so a reader is handed the review standing even though the applied standing is unstated — and that pin is what resolves G16 v2's own reviewStatus still reading AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW. 'Live' is also established vocabulary here rather than a claim of application: G16 v2's own namedCorpusNote, which this catalog quotes verbatim, opens 'Live harness-cell punctuation', meaning the current register cell.
advisories.residue: A reader who takes 'Live' at face value could infer the specification is settled and applied, which it is not, and the asymmetry with the v16 entry makes that inference easier. One clause — CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, not QUALIFIED — would close it, and it is the wording the sibling artifacts in this family use for cited harness specifications.

advisories.title: Live file 08 still describes the G16 harness as not authored, now the fourth row in this family
advisories.detail: The DR-G16 row reads 'named: harness.DR-G16.ci-isolation-integration (D-086; not authored; not QUALIFIED)' while G16 v2 exists with a Claude ACCEPT 0/0 that the subject pins and I verified. As with the sibling cases, this subject neither creates nor engages the disagreement: it claims no authoring close, and G16 v2's own whatThisCloses makes OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC conditional on being independently accepted and later D-000-recorded, which has not happened. So the correction is owed by that recording, not by this catalog.
advisories.standing: Recorded chiefly to complete a pattern. This is the fourth register row in the same condition — DR-G09, DR-G15, DR-G26 and now DR-G16 — where an authored harness specification sits behind a cell that still reads 'not authored', and condition 4 carries the same blanket phrase across all 26 required gates. Four separate advisories on four subjects is worse than one disposition; the coordinator should consider handling the family in a single act. Directed at the coordinator, not a defect of the subject.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 advisories. Twenty-two attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject bceb4d16 at 0444, 9808 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-121 token OPEN; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All six cited digests reproduce, COORD pinned at the live value, and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head as the artifact's own clause requires. This artifact claims nothing except that it quotes accurately, so quotation was tested by equality: eleven strings — three memberVerbatim, three exactByteIntent, three passProperty, the corpus note and the v16 standing — each equal to its live G16 v2 source by ==, with the three class ids matching in order and the namedCorpusNotAuthored list matching as an ordered list including its multiplication sign. The longest quote, the aggregate-release exactByteIntent, matches to its final character. No truncation, no paraphrase. The identifier attack is the one designed to catch a careless reviewer, and it is refuted by position rather than by absence: G16-12, IR-1 and IR-4 are present, but only inside the single field I verified byte-equal to the source, whose own words mark them cited-not-applied. I also disclose a false positive of my own — my pattern flagged FX-AUTHORING at four sites, all of them the tail of OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING, an obligation id I confirmed exists in monorepo-leftover-join.v1, so the raw count is not four adoptions. Nothing is invented: no fixture bytes, with NOT-AUTHORED on every class; no CI encoding, since every YAML, cache, path-filter and vendor mention is either a quoted denial of authority or the artifact's own refusal; no numeric window, with all eight bare integers outside quoted fields enumerated and accounted for; and no status token, with zero case-insensitive occurrences of SATISFIED and the single QUALIFIED hit being the lowercase word inside a quote. Two structural checks that could have looked like defects both resolve in the subject's favour. Its registerRow DR-121 differs from G16 v2's DR-G16, but G16 v2 says in its own bytes that it is the gate row itself, and DR-121 is where the continued obligation lives — the same two-row convention I verified on G26. And its scope covers only OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING while the leftover-join also carries OBL-CI-ENCODING-RESERVED; that scope is stated in the purpose and not encroached on, since refusing to invent CI tooling is exactly what the reserved obligation holds. I probed for a fourth corpus class and found none: namedCorpusNotAuthored is the only key of its kind, holds three members, and G16 v2's other unauthored markers resolve to the register naming standing, naming v6, or text this catalog already carries verbatim. Two advisories, neither barring acceptance. The first is the only wording residue: G16 v2 is called the 'Live G16 specification' with no note that it is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING, while v16 — the artifact the catalog must not apply — gets its standing quoted in full. Nothing the catalog claims depends on G16 v2 being applied, and its review is pinned with the verdict stated, so this stays advisory; one clause would close it. The second completes a pattern rather than reporting a new fact: DR-G16 is now the fourth register row after DR-G09, DR-G15 and DR-G26 where an authored harness specification sits behind a cell reading 'not authored'. Four advisories on four subjects is worse than one disposition, and the coordinator should consider handling the family in a single act.
